t.1.55.1: Thus addressed by Vasiṣṭha, the mighty Viśvāmitra raised the fiery weapon of Agni and said, "Stand, stand!"
t.1.55.2: The blessed Vasiṣṭha, in anger, spoke these words: "O base kṣatriya, here I stand; whatever power you have, display it."
t.1.55.3: I myself shall destroy your pride in your weapon, O Gādhija. What is your warrior's might compared with the great might of a brahmin?
t.1.55.4: Behold my divine power of brahman, O disgrace of the kṣatriyas! Then the dreadful and supreme fire-weapon of that son of Gādhi…
t.1.55.6: Enraged, the son of Gādhi hurled the Aiṣīka weapon as well, and the Mānava, the Mohana, the Gāndharva, and likewise the Svāpana.
t.1.55.5: That weapon was quelled by the Brahmadaṇḍa, as the force of fire is quenched by water. And the Vāruṇa, the Raudra, the Aindra, and likewise the Pāśupata weapons…
t.1.55.8: The noose of Brahmā, the noose of Kāla, and the noose of Varuṇa too, the beloved Pināka missile, and likewise the two thunderbolts, the dry and the wet.
t.1.55.7: The Jṛmbhaṇa and the Mohana, the Saṃtāpana and the Vilāpana, the Śoṣaṇa and the Dāraṇa, and the Vajra weapon, very hard to overcome.
t.1.55.10: He hurled the Vāyavya and the Mathana, and likewise the missile Hayaśiras, the pair of Śaktis, and likewise the Kaṅkāla and the Musala.
t.1.55.9: Then the Daṇḍa missile and the Paiśāca, and likewise the Krauñca missile; the Dharmacakra, the Kālacakra, and likewise the Viṣṇucakra.
t.1.55.11: The great Vaidyādhara missile, and then the dreadful Kāla missile, the terrible Triśūla missile, the Kāpāla, and then the Kaṅkaṇa.
t.1.55.14: Seeing that weapon raised, the gods with Agni at their head, the divine seers, and the Gandharvas together with the great serpents were thrown into alarm.
t.1.55.12: O Raghunandana, he hurled all these weapons at Vasiṣṭha, the foremost of those who chant prayers, and it was a marvel indeed.
t.1.55.13: The son of Brahmā swallows all of them with his staff; and when they had been quelled, the son of Gādhi hurled the Brahmāstra.
t.1.55.15: When the Brahmāstra was hurled, the three worlds were struck with terror; yet that exceedingly dreadful weapon of Brahmā, too, the sage overpowered by his own brahmic might.
t.1.55.16: O Rāghava, Vasiṣṭha swallows everything with his Brahmadaṇḍa. Of the great-souled Vasiṣṭha, as he was swallowing the Brahmāstra…
t.1.55.17: In all the pores of the great-souled Vasiṣṭha there appeared a fierce and exceedingly dreadful form that bewildered the three worlds.
t.1.55.18: Like rays from a fire whose flames are wreathed in smoke, they flew forth, and the Brahmadaṇḍa raised in Vasiṣṭha's hand blazed up.
t.1.55.19: He stood like the fire of Time at the end of the world, blazing without smoke, like a second rod of Yama. Then the hosts of sages praised Vasiṣṭha, the best of those who recite prayers.
t.1.55.20: Unfailing is your power, O brahmin; restrain your fiery energy by your own energy. Viśvāmitra, great in austerities, has been subdued by you, O brahmin.
t.1.55.21: Be gracious, O best of those who murmur prayers, and let the worlds be freed from their distress. Thus addressed, the greatly radiant one of great austerities grew calm.
t.1.55.22: Viśvāmitra, humbled, heaved a deep sigh and said this: "Fie upon the might of a kṣatriya! The might of brahminical splendor alone is true might."
t.1.55.24: I shall undertake great austerity, which indeed brings about the state of a brahmin.
t.1.55.23: By a single brahmadaṇḍa all my weapons have been destroyed. Having reflected upon this, I, with senses and mind made tranquil, shall turn to austerity.
